theater: 埃及三角洲與昔蘭尼加

battle.name: 傭兵戰爭
battle.theater: 埃及三角洲與昔蘭尼加
battle.brief: 公元前240年秋，托勒密三世在加沙戰敗，欠餉的傭兵在埃及三角洲叛變，約兩萬人的步兵西進昔蘭尼加，聯合當地居民與利比亞部族；托勒密先遣艦隊馳援，卻在馬雷奧提斯湖淺灘觸礁覆沒，翌年再以大軍平叛。卡面的埃及長矛屬早王朝型制，並未出現在此役，但它標示的長矛技術，正是雙方步兵近戰的骨幹。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場戰爭是公元前240年托勒密王國內部由軍隊叛變引發的內戰，同時也是希臘化世界一次典型的僱傭兵危機：開戰的雙方並非兩個主權國家，而是一支武裝叛軍與它的前雇主。叛變方主力是托勒密王國軍中的僱傭兵，其中加利亞人（高盧人）與希臘人居多，另有色雷斯人、克里特弓手與來自小亞細亞的散兵；羅馬與迦太基的戰爭告一段落之後，地中海的職業兵市場過剩，這批四處找活路的人才敢在王宮門口舉旗。加入他們的是昔蘭尼加的本地居民：五城地區的市民對托勒密家的長久統治積怨已久，利比亞游牧部族則趁亂南下，與叛軍合流。受災一方是托勒密王朝的中央政府、埃及本國軍隊，以及被滯留在埃及境內的其他外邦士兵；托勒密三世以王室直屬部隊、象軍與分遣隊伍應戰，把戰場從尼羅河三角洲一路推到昔蘭尼加沿海。這場衝突沒有第三國直接介入，但它牽動了塞琉古與托勒密爭奪地中海東部的大局，也牽動了希臘本土的局勢。
countriesEn: This war was a civil conflict inside the Ptolemaic kingdom that broke out in 240 BC as a mutiny of the army, and at the same time a classic mercenary crisis of the Hellenistic world: the two sides were not two sovereign states but an armed rebellion and its former employer. The heart of the rebel force was made up of mercenaries in Ptolemaic pay, in the main Galatians (Celts) and Greeks, with Thracians, Cretan archers and stragglers from Asia Minor mixed in. Once the wars of Rome and Carthage had come to an end, the Mediterranean market for professional soldiers was glutted with men out of work, and it was precisely such rootless men who dared to raise the flag at the gate of a royal palace. Joining them were the inhabitants of Cyrenaica: the citizens of the Pentapolis had long resented the rule of the Ptolemy dynasty, while the Libyan nomads moved south and linked up with the mutineers. On the other side stood the central government of the Ptolemaic dynasty, the native Egyptian troops, and the foreign soldiers stranded on Egyptian soil. Ptolemy III answered with troops of the royal household, with war elephants and with detached columns, and carried the fighting from the Nile delta all the way to the coast of Cyrenaica. No third state intervened directly, but the conflict was tied into the larger struggle between the Seleucids and the Ptolemies for the eastern Mediterranean and into the situation in mainland Greece.
people: 主線人物以波利比阿斯《歷史》卷二的記載最為完整。叛軍方面留下的名字有限：傭兵隊伍自行推舉最高指揮者，並把本地人推上戰線，古代文本對這批首領的姓名與出身記錄模糊，只能確認他們由傭兵將領與昔蘭尼加本地首領混合組成。托勒密方面的名字比較清楚：國王的兄弟馬加斯（Magas）原鎮守昔蘭尼加，被懷疑煽動傭兵叛亂而在宮廷中被處死，顯示朝廷內部對這批武裝早已猜忌；波利比阿斯記下國王先派出的將領帕麥涅（Pammene）與卡利克勒斯（Kallikles），率一支規模不大的先遣部隊前往昔蘭尼加，又記下王室中有人出面為傭兵說情，使國王一度同意他們的條件。真正決定戰局的仍是國王本人：托勒密三世第二次派出遠多於第一批的步兵、騎兵與艦隊，親自率隊西進，把叛軍逼入海邊的堡塞，終於平定叛亂。
peopleEn: The main line of personalities is best preserved in Book 2 of Polybius' Histories. On the rebel side few names survive: the mercenary ranks elected their own supreme commanders and pushed local men to the front, and the ancient text is vague about the names and backgrounds of these leaders, confirming only that they were a mixture of mercenary officers and Cyrenaican notables. On the Ptolemaic side the names are clearer. The king's brother Magas, who had been stationed at Cyrene, was suspected of inciting the mutiny and was put to death in the court, which shows that the government had long mistrusted this armed mass. Polybius records the commanders Ptolemy first sent out, Pammene and Kallikles, with a modest advance force, and he also records that someone in the royal family interceded for the mercenaries, so that the king for a time agreed to their terms. The figure who actually decided the campaign was the king himself: Ptolemy III despatched a second army of foot, horse and ships far larger than the first, led it westward in person, drove the rebels into a fortress by the sea, and finally ended the revolt.
kits: 卡面兵器是「埃及長矛」：早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭以繩束綁在木杆上，用於守城垣與野戰的戳刺、格擋。這件兵器出自公元前3200年前後的早王朝，屬於「金屬矛頭加木杆」這條最古老的冷兵器譜系，比這場戰爭早了近三千年，並未出現在昔蘭尼加的戰場上；把它放進這場戰爭，是要標示「矛」這條技術脈絡在希臘化時代仍佔著步兵骨幹的位置。實際參戰的長兵器是薩里沙長矛（sarissa），槍身可達六公尺上下，須雙手握持，槍尾有可插入地面的鐵刺，密集方陣的推進力量正來自這種長矛；輕裝步兵與散兵用短刺矛，遠擲則用皮洛姆式標槍（pilum）與石彈。盾牌以圓盾為主，配合亞麻布甲與鱗甲，投擲武器是弓與雙管投石器。托勒密方面的特色是象軍與攻城器：攻城槌、投石塔與配重裝置是東地中海的常規配置，用來對付昔蘭尼加的石砌城牆。叛軍方面以傭兵的制式裝備為基礎，加上利比亞輕騎兵、克里特弓手與昔蘭尼加的小型戰船；海運是這場戰爭的關鍵，糧秣、攻城器與援兵都靠船，港口的得失等於戰役的一半。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Egyptian spear: a spear of the Early Dynastic period, with a copper or bronze head lashed to a wooden shaft, used to stab and to brace in the defence of walls and in the open field. It comes from around 3200 BC, belongs to the oldest family of cold weapons, a metal head bound to a wooden shaft, and predates this war by nearly three thousand years; it never appeared on any battlefield of Cyrenaica. It is placed in this war because it marks the line of technical development of the spear, which still occupied the place of backbone in the infantry of the Hellenistic age. The long weapon actually fought with was the sarissa, a pike of up to about six metres, held with both hands and fitted with an iron spike at the butt for planting in the ground, and it was the sarissa that gave the dense phalanx its pushing power; light infantry and peltasts carried short stabbing spears, and the missile arm was the pilum and the sling stone. Shields were mostly round, worn with linen cuirasses and scale armour, and the missile troops used the bow and the double-acting catapult. The hallmark of the Ptolemaic side was the elephant corps and the siege train: battering rams, stone-throwing towers and counterweight devices were standard in the eastern Mediterranean and were used against the stone walls of Cyrene. The rebels fought with the standard kit of mercenaries, reinforced by Libyan light horse, Cretan archers and the small war galleys of Cyrenaica. Sea transport was the hinge of the whole war: grain, siege engines and reinforcements all moved by ship, and the fate of the harbours was half the fate of the campaign.
tactics: 這場叛亂的基本形態是「整支軍隊帶著裝備離開雇主」，這與希臘城邦常見的短期僱傭不同：一支兩萬人上下的步兵集群一旦脫離國王的支付與指揮，就必須自己找糧食、自己決定方向。叛軍進入昔蘭尼加後採三段式推進：先靠本地嚮導在沿海道路與內陸綠洲之間轉移，避開開闊的三角洲正面；再與當地人合流，攻取五城地區的城市，奪取糧倉、船隻與港口；最後以海路與騎兵偵察托勒密援軍的到來時間。托勒密最初的解法是速決：海軍把步兵直接運進昔蘭尼加，結果因為夜航誤入馬雷奧提斯湖的淺灘而全軍覆沒，這是整場戰爭最關鍵的一課——亞歷山德里亞附近的潮汐與沙洲只有熟悉當地的引航者曉得。第二次作戰改為陸海並行：步兵沿海岸推進，逐點清剿叛軍據點，騎兵封鎖內陸，艦隊切斷海路，最後把叛軍騎兵趕入海邊堡塞後攻破，用封鎖與消耗取代正面決戰。整體而言，這是一場以補給線、港口與海路為核心的戰爭。
tacticsEn: The basic form of this revolt was an entire army leaving its employer with its equipment, which is quite different from the short-term hire common in the Greek city-states: once a cluster of some twenty thousand footmen is cut off from the king's pay and command, it must find its own food and decide its own direction. After entering Cyrenaica the rebels advanced in three stages. They first used local guides to move between the coastal road and the inland oases, avoiding the open ground of the delta; then they joined with the local population and took the cities of the Pentapolis, seizing granaries, ships and harbours; last they used the sea routes and their cavalry to watch for the arrival of Ptolemy's reinforcements. Ptolemy's first answer was speed: the fleet carried the infantry straight into Cyrenaica, and the whole expedition was lost because the ships, sailing at night, struck the shoals of the lake Mareotis. That was the sharpest lesson of the war, for the tides and sandbanks off Alexandria were known only to local pilots. The second campaign was run on land and sea together: the infantry advanced along the coast, clearing the rebel posts one by one, the cavalry sealed the interior, the fleet cut the sea route, and in the end the rebel cavalry were driven into a fortress by the shore and then stormed, blockade and exhaustion taking the place of a set-piece decision. As a whole this was a war fought around supply lines, harbours and sea routes.
data: 能夠核實的數字有限，以下幾組最為可靠。時間：戰爭始於公元前240年秋季加沙戰敗之後，傭兵在埃及境內起事，前239年托勒密三世第二次出兵，到前238年平定，前後約兩至三年，是希臘化世界規模最大的一次傭兵叛亂。兵力：波利比阿斯把叛軍步兵記為約兩萬人，騎兵以利比亞輕騎為主，數量在數千；托勒密第一批派出的只是數千人規模的先遣隊，由帕麥涅與卡利克勒斯率領，第二批才是主力，人數以萬計，另有數十頭象與一支艦隊。艦隊：托勒密方面的船隻為數十艘，在馬雷奧提斯湖一次觸礁即告全毀，史料記載溺斃與被俘者以數千計，說明一次海路事故就足以改寫整場戰役的進程。距離：亞歷山德里亞至昔蘭尼加的沿海航程約八百公里，五城地區內部多為土路，車隊一日行程有限，糧秣靠沿海船運與當地徵集，冬季地中海常有逆風，停航可達數週。缺失的部分：叛軍與守軍的逐日傷亡、攻城器數量、象軍頭數與城內存糧都沒有留下可靠記錄，古代作者往往只以「極多」形容，不能當作精確數字使用。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are few, and the following groups are the most reliable. Timing: the war began in the autumn of 240 BC after the defeat at Gaza, the mutiny breaking out inside Egypt; Ptolemy III launched his second expedition in 239 BC, and the revolt was settled in 238 BC, roughly two to three years in all, and it was the largest mercenary revolt in the Hellenistic world. Numbers: Polybius records the rebel infantry at about twenty thousand, with the cavalry mainly Libyan light horse numbering in the thousands; the first force Ptolemy sent was only an advance detachment of a few thousand men under Pammene and Kallikles, while the second was the main body, in the tens of thousands, with some dozens of elephants and a fleet. The fleet: the Ptolemaic ships numbered in the tens, and a single grounding in the lake Mareotis destroyed them all, the ancient account putting the drowned and the captured in the thousands, which shows how one accident on the water could rewrite the whole course of a campaign. Distance: the coastal passage from Alexandria to Cyrene is about eight hundred kilometres; inside the Pentapolis the roads are mostly dirt tracks and a wagon team makes limited daily progress; grain came by coastal shipping and by requisition on the spot, and the winter gales in the Mediterranean could stop the shipping for weeks. What is missing: day-by-day casualties on both sides, the number of siege engines, the count of elephants and the grain stored in the cities leave no reliable record; the ancient writers tend to say only that there were very many, and such phrases cannot be used as exact figures.
cause: 起因可以分四層。最下層是托勒密王朝的財政與軍制：國王在加沙戰敗前已傾力西征，戰敗後軍隊潰散、戰利品散失，國庫難以同時支付留用兵員的薪餉與戰俘的贖金；而希臘化王國的常備軍本來建立在按季發餉、外包徵募之上，付款一旦中斷，整支軍隊立刻變成武裝團體。第二層是地中海僱傭兵市場的收縮：迦太基與羅馬的戰爭結束後，職業兵大量失業，願意接受任何付錢雇主的兵源過剩，這批人因此敢於在受雇國家的王宮門口舉旗。第三層是托勒密二世留下的王位裂痕：他晚年改立其子托勒密四世為共治者，賽浦蒂斯王朝的繼承由此長期混亂，王室成員彼此猜忌，鎮守昔蘭尼加的馬加斯被處死即出自這條裂痕。最後是直接引爆：前240年秋，戰敗的訊息與軍餉積欠同時傳到埃及，傭兵在三角洲的駐地集結，殺死督導的軍官，奪取營地裡的武器與攻城器械，然後整隊西行，把一次欠餉糾紛變成了一場遷徙式的叛亂。
causeEn: The causes can be read on four levels. The lowest is the finances and the military system of the Ptolemaic dynasty: the king had committed everything to the western campaign before Gaza, and after the defeat the army broke up and the spoils were lost, so that the treasury could not at once pay the soldiers it kept and the ransoms it owed. The standing army of the Hellenistic kingdoms rested in the first place on paying wages by the season and on hiring out recruitment; once the payments stopped, a whole army turned at once into an armed mob. The second level is the contraction of the Mediterranean mercenary market: with the wars of Rome and Carthage over, professional soldiers were largely unemployed, and the surplus of men willing to take service from any payer who would pay is what allowed this crowd to raise the banner before the palace of the state that had employed them. The third level is the succession fracture left by Ptolemy II, who late in life made his son Ptolemy IV co-regent, leaving the succession of the dynasty in chronic confusion and the members of the royal house suspicious of one another; the execution of Magas, the governor of Cyrene, came straight out of this fracture. The last level is the trigger: in the autumn of 240 BC the news of the defeat and the arrears of pay reached Egypt together, the mercenaries mustered in their cantonments in the delta, killed the officers who supervised them, seized the arms and the siege engines in the camps, and then marched west in formation, turning a dispute over unpaid wages into a migration in arms.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接結果，是托勒密王朝失去對昔蘭尼加的控制，國王的兄弟被處死，寶貴的象軍與海軍在一次事故中損失殆盡，王室財政與軍隊的信用都受重創。更深遠的影響在東地中海的政治格局上：前240年同時，塞琉古王安條克三世在腓尼基與科埃勒敘利亞得手，前238年的帕尼翁之戰更讓他取得腓尼基沿岸的大片據點；托勒密三世被傭兵叛亂釘在埃及與昔蘭尼加，等於把希臘化東方的樞紐讓給了塞琉古，直到前227年克里莫尼德戰爭與馬其頓的介入才被逆轉。傭兵在這場戰爭中的表現又反過來影響希臘：前241至前237年的第三次聖戰中爭奪德爾斐的戰線，同樣靠四處漂泊的傭兵支撐，僱傭兵是否存在成了城邦外交的一個變數。托勒密王國此後更倚重本土步兵、馬其頓老兵與象軍的混合編制，軍費籌措與兵源管理也長期受此案刺激，開始更講究以授地與授予公民權把傭兵綁在王朝一邊。武器史上的對照同樣清楚：早王朝的短刺矛與希臘化時代的六公尺薩里沙長矛，恰好是「金屬矛頭加木杆」這條譜系的兩端，前者守城垣，後者決定方陣的推進速度。
impactEn: The immediate result of the war was that the Ptolemaic dynasty lost control of Cyrene, that the king's brother was executed, that the precious elephants and fleet were nearly wiped out in a single accident, and that both the finances of the crown and the credit of its army were damaged. The deeper effects belong to the politics of the eastern Mediterranean: at the same time as 240 BC the Seleucid king Antiochus III made gains in Phoenicia and Coele-Syria, and the battle of Panium in 238 BC gave him a large stretch of the Phoenician coast; Ptolemy III, pinned by the mercenary revolt in Egypt and Cyrenaica, effectively handed the hinge of the Hellenistic east to the Seleucids, and this was not reversed until the Chremonidean War of 227 BC and the intervention of Macedon. The behaviour of mercenaries in this war in turn affected Greece: between 241 and 237 BC the Third Sacred War was fought over Delphi and was likewise sustained by mercenaries drifting from one employer to another, so the presence or absence of hired troops became one of the variables in polis diplomacy. The Ptolemaic kingdom afterwards relied more heavily on a mixed establishment of native infantry, Macedonian veterans and elephants, and the financing of the army and the management of its manpower were long stimulated by this case, with more attention paid to tying mercenaries to the dynasty by grants of land and grants of citizenship. The contrast in the history of weapons is equally clear: the short stabbing spear of the Early Dynastic period and the six-metre sarissa of the Hellenistic age mark the two ends of the same family, a metal head on a wooden shaft, the former used to hold a wall, the latter deciding the speed at which a phalanx advanced.
result: 公元前238年，叛亂被平定。托勒密三世的第二次遠征在昔蘭尼加海岸與叛軍決戰，叛軍騎兵被逐入海邊的堡塞，史家記其名為「勒凱」一帶，國王隨後攻破該堡，殘部或死於堡內，或在退向海邊時被殲滅、俘虜。留在埃及的傭兵被遣散或收編，昔蘭尼加的抵抗力量瓦解，五城地區重新回到托勒密家手中；國王其後重整當地的城市編制，把其中一座以自己的名字命名為托勒密里斯，五城聯邦的行政框架由此定型。對叛軍而言，他們既沒有得到獨立國家，也沒有取得土地安置，只換來一次長途西征與全軍覆沒；他們留下的唯一政治成果，是迫使托勒密王朝正視傭兵必須有餉、有安置這個問題，此後的薪餉支付與土地授給成為希臘化僱傭關係的標準配備。整場戰爭歷時約兩至三年，是希臘化世界規模最大的一次傭兵叛亂，也因此成了後世講述傭兵之亂時最常被引用的範本。
resultEn: The revolt was crushed in 238 BC. Ptolemy III's second expedition met the rebels in a battle off the coast of Cyrenaica; the rebel cavalry were driven into a fortress by the sea, which the ancient account places at a place called Leuke, and the king then stormed it, the survivors being either killed inside or destroyed or captured on the way back toward the sea. The mercenaries who remained in Egypt were dispersed or taken back into service, the resistance in Cyrenaica collapsed, and the Pentapolis returned to the Ptolemies; the king later reorganised the cities of the district and gave one of them his own name as Ptolemais, so that the administrative frame of the five-city league was fixed. For the rebels the outcome brought neither an independent state nor any allotment of land, only a long march west and the destruction of their army; the one political result they left was to force the Ptolemaic dynasty to take seriously that mercenaries must be paid and must be settled, after which cash wages and grants of land became the standard equipment of Hellenistic employment. The whole war lasted some two to three years, was the largest mercenary revolt in the Hellenistic world, and for that reason became the most frequently cited model whenever later writers told of a war of mercenaries.
